explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem gives an explicit formula for the counit of the library's own `tensorSheafAdjunction`, the extension-of-scalars adjunction for sheaves of modules along `theta : A ⟶ B`. It evaluates that counit on the sheafified section `b • (1 ⊗ n)` and gets `b • n`. Its content therefore lies in the library's own definitions: `tensorPresheaf`, `tensorUnitSection`, `sheafCounitPresheafMap` and `tensorSheafAdjunction`. The proof only uses the generic Mathlib lemma `Adjunction.homEquiv_unit` (on the sheafification adjunction) together with the library's own lemmas. I searched Mathlib's `ModuleCat/Presheaf` and `ModuleCat/Sheaf` directories. The pullback/pushforward adjunctions there (`PullbackContinuous`, `Presheaf/Pullback`) are along continuous functors, not change of rings by an explicit tensor product. None of them gives this formula for a counit evaluated on elements.
